view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

task.detail: Y*(x)=argmin_y g(x,y); Phi(x)=min_{y in Y*(x)} f(x,y), with the optimistic minimum attained.
description_paragraphs: Consider the optimistic bilevel problem $Y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}g(x,y)$, $\Phi(x)=\min_{y\in Y^*(x)}f(x,y)$, and seek stationarity of $\min_x\Phi(x)$. Multiple global lower-level solutions are allowed; the defining minima must be attained. Among lower-level minimizers, select one minimizing the upper-level objective.

model.selection: Optimistic over all global lower minimizers; no arbitrary chosen branch and no pessimistic max.
model.uniform_PL: For every x and every t in [0,t_bar], h_t(x,y)=g(x,y)+t f(x,y) attains a minimum and satisfies ||grad_y h_t||^2 >= 2 mu_PL (h_t-min_y h_t), with the same mu_PL>0.
model.regularity: f,g have jointly Lipschitz gradients and Hessians with declared finite budgets L_f,L_g,rho_f,rho_g; f(x,.) is C_f-Lipschitz. This is population regularity, not per-sample smoothness.
model.initialization: Phi(x0)-inf Phi<=Delta<infinity; dist(y0,Y*(x0))<=R_y<infinity; all those budgets are public.
model.derived_property: Smoothness and differentiability of the optimistic Phi are obtained under the uniform perturbed-PL assumptions; PL of g alone is insufficient.
description_paragraphs: For every $x$ and $t\in[0,\bar t]$, the perturbed lower-level objective $h_t(x,y)=g(x,y)+t f(x,y)$ attains its minimum and satisfies $\|\nabla_yh_t\|^2\ge2\mu_{\mathrm{PL}}(h_t-\min_yh_t)$ with the same constant $\mu_{\mathrm{PL}}>0$.

The joint gradient and Hessian of $f,g$ have finite Lipschitz budgets $L_f,L_g,\rho_f,\rho_g$; $f(x,\cdot)$ is $C_f$-Lipschitz. Also $\Phi(x_0)-\inf\Phi\le\Delta$ and $\operatorname{dist}(y_0,Y^*(x_0))\le R_y$. These are population assumptions, not samplewise assumptions.
model.outer_geometry: The reduced objective may be nonconvex. Its differentiability or local Lipschitz regularity is specified by the model and accuracy measure.

operations: Choose h=f or g and point (x,y); receive G_h(x,y) with conditional mean grad h and conditional second centered moment <=sigma_h^2.
oracle.coupling: Fresh independent samples at every call; no cross-point reuse. One selected full gradient per call.
description_paragraphs: At any $(x,y)$, choose $h=f$ or $g$ and receive the fresh full-gradient sample $G_h$. Conditional on history $\mathcal{H}$ and the query, $\mathbb{E}[G_h\mid\mathcal{H}]=\nabla h$ and $\mathbb{E}[\|G_h-\nabla h\|^2\mid\mathcal{H}]\le\sigma_h^2$ hold. Calls use independent fresh samples with no cross-point reuse.
Dimensions, budget, and initial point are public. No direct inner-solution, branch-selection, hypergradient, or second-order interface is supplied.
Return a single outer point $\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$, possibly a randomized historical point or an unqueried point. No certificate is required.
The criterion is $\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat x)\|$. Differentiability follows from the uniform perturbed-PL model, not from a PL condition on $g$ alone.

description_paragraphs: The budget is $N=N_{\nabla f}+N_{\nabla g}$. Each sample costs one unit, under a fixed worst-case budget including all initialization and inner-loop calls.
